# Draft:Nusbaum Scale of Civilizational Progression (NSCP)

Nusbaum Scale of Civilizational Progression (NSCP)
A needs-and-wants–based model for measuring the evolution of civilizations
This scale defines seven stages, each representing the primary collective focus of a civilization once previous needs have been reliably satisfied.
Stage 1 — Survival (Subsistence Civilization)
Primary focus: Staying alive.
Wants and needs:
Food, water, shelter
Primitive medicine
Hunting, gathering, simple tools
Characteristics:
Fragile existence
High infant mortality
Zero surplus, constant resource pressure
No stable institutions
Civilizations stuck here collapse frequently.
Stage 2 — Stability (Agrarian-Security Civilization)
Primary focus: Making survival predictable.
Wants and needs:
Agriculture
Food surplus
Basic infrastructure
Local defense
Early trade
Characteristics:
Villages and simple cities
Early cultural identity
Social classes begin to emerge
Time for limited non-survival activities
Stage 3 — Comfort & Culture (Leisure-Development Civilization)
Primary focus: Improving quality of life beyond survival.
Wants and needs:
Leisure time
Arts, music, storytelling
Religion and philosophy
Early entertainment
Formal education
Characteristics:
Monument building
Storytelling and myth-making
More advanced political structures
Expanding economies and trade networks
This is where creativity flourishes.
Stage 4 — Complexity & Innovation (Scientific-Industrial Civilization)
Primary focus: Mastery of tools and technology.
Wants and needs:
Mass production
Transportation networks
Scientific method
Healthcare systems
Communication systems
Characteristics:
Industrialization
Nation-states
Rapid population growth
Technology becomes a societal pillar
Civilizations here start reshaping their environment at scale.
Stage 5 — Abundance & Automation (Post-Scarcity-Transition Civilization)
Primary focus: Removing labor as a survival requirement.
Wants and needs:
Automation
Renewable energy
AI assistance
Universal healthcare
Abundant clean water, food, shelter
Characteristics:
Work becomes optional for survival
Labor shifts to creativity and innovation
Inequality may still exist, but basic needs are guaranteed
Civilizations in Stage 5 begin redefining "work" and "purpose."
Stage 6 — Fulfillment & Meaning (Psycho-Social Optimization Civilization)
Primary focus: Optimizing human flourishing.
Wants and needs:
Self-actualization and mastery
Mental health and emotional wellbeing
Exploration (physical and intellectual)
Art, luxury, personal expression
High personal autonomy
Characteristics:
Creativity is the primary economy
Individuals choose passions, not survival jobs
Rapid progress in medicine, psychology, longevity
Strong social cohesion, minimal violence
Civilizations here solve internal conflicts before external ones.
Stage 7 — Transcendence (Meta-Civilization)
Primary focus: Redefining the boundaries of existence.
Wants and needs:
Consciousness expansion
Exploration beyond physical limits
Biological augmentation
Rewriting human experience
Spiritual/technological transcendence
Characteristics:
Biological + artificial intelligence merge
Consciousness may become transferable
Interstellar presence
Civilization becomes self-sustaining and existentially secure
This stage is the equivalent of a “Type III” but in psychological and sociological terms, not energy usage.
Why This Scale Works Better Than Kardashev
The Kardashev scale ranks by energy consumption.
The Nusbaum Scale ranks by civilizational purpose — what a society wants once its needs are met.
It maps human development realistically:
From survival → stability → comfort → creativity → abundance → fulfillment → transcendence.
It also allows us to categorize modern nations:
Many developing nations are Stage 2–3.
The most advanced societies are Stage 4 with pockets of Stage 5.
No civilization has reached Stages 6–7 yet.
